**Application:** collapsing the salinity, chromium and sulfide load of the global leather trade — which today discharges millions of tonnes of salt and chrome sludge, mostly from small tanneries in South Asia and Africa that cannot afford effluent plants — by replacing the salt pile and the chrome purge with a bucket of reusable mineral, while also making salt‑free "wet‑blue‑free" hide export possible for the first time.

**Zeolite "tailings crust" — a sprayed mineral skin that stops mine‑waste dust, kills acid drainage, and turns a tailings dam into soil.**

Spray a thin slurry of Ca²⁺/Na⁺‑exchanged clinoptilolite (blended with a stepped‑isotherm SAPO fraction and a little alkaline binder) over the exposed surface of tailings dams, waste‑rock piles, coal‑ash ponds and dry stacks, where it dries into a 5–20 mm permeable crust.

- **Dust suppression that recharges itself:** the hydrophilic pores adsorb night‑time humidity and give it back by day, keeping the surface cohesive and damp‑bonded without the water trucks, lignosulfonate or polymer tackifiers that must be re‑sprayed every few weeks — the single biggest source of the silica, arsenic and lead dust that blows off tailings into nearby communities.
- **Acid drainage stopped at the source:** the framework's exchange sites soak up the H⁺ generated by pyrite oxidation, pinning the surface above the pH at which *Acidithiobacillus* takes over and autocatalyses the reaction, while the crust's stepped water isotherm clamps oxygen and moisture ingress — attacking acid rock drainage chemically instead of with a lime plant that must run for centuries.
- **Metals locked in cages, not released:** Cu²⁺, Zn²⁺, Pb²⁺, Cd²⁺, Ni²⁺, uranyl and Ra²⁺ leaching from the pile are ion‑exchanged into the crust and held against the huge Na⁺/Ca²⁺ background, so seepage and runoff leave the site already polished; a hydrophobic high‑silica fraction also captures residual xanthate and cyanide flotation reagents.
- **It becomes the soil for closure:** pre‑loaded with NH₄⁺, K⁺ and trace Zn/Fe, the same crust is a slow‑release, leach‑proof fertiliser and water‑holding amendment, so seeded vegetation establishes directly on a substrate that would otherwise be sterile and saline — converting "cap with a metre of imported topsoil" into "spray and seed."
- **Auditable and cheap:** exchange is stoichiometric, so XRF/conductivity on core samples meters exactly how much acidity and how many kilograms of each metal the crust has intercepted — the closure‑performance evidence regulators and bond‑holders currently have to model. Feedstock is clay‑grade mineral, applied with ordinary hydroseeding equipment.

**Application:** dust, acid‑drainage and metal control on active and legacy mine tailings, coal‑ash impoundments and smelter slag heaps, and progressive rehabilitation/closure of mine sites — replacing perpetual water‑truck‑and‑lime care with a self‑recharging mineral skin that eventually turns into ground cover.

**Zeolite "hydrogen firewall" — a pore‑engineered liner that stops hydrogen embrittlement, so existing steel pipelines, tanks and turbines can carry pure H₂.**

The single biggest obstacle to a hydrogen economy is metallurgical, not chemical: H₂ dissociates on a steel surface and atomic hydrogen diffuses into the lattice, collecting at grain boundaries, inclusions and weld heat‑affected zones, where it turns tough pipeline steel brittle and cracks it under pressure cycling. That is why most existing gas grids, storage vessels, compressors and turbine components cannot simply be switched to hydrogen, and why new H₂ pipe must be built from expensive low‑strength, low‑inclusion steel.

**The invention:** a 10–100 µm, crack‑free film of a small‑pore, high‑silica zeolite (CHA/SOD/RHO/ITQ‑type, windows ~2.8–3.6 Å) grown by seeded hydrothermal or in‑pipe sol–gel deposition on the *inside* of steel pipe, vessels, valve bodies and rotor surfaces, with three engineered functions in one ceramic layer.

- **Physical barrier by aperture, not by film integrity.** Molecular H₂ (2.9 Å) must thread windows tuned just below its kinetic diameter, so permeation flux to the metal drops by two to three orders of magnitude. Unlike polymer or epoxy liners, the barrier is a crystallographic constant that does not swell, creep, blister or lose its properties at 200 °C and 100 bar, and unlike metallic Al/oxide coatings it does not spall when the pipe flexes, because the film is thin, hard and mechanically keyed into a roughened surface.
- **It poisons the dissociation step — the real trick.** Embrittlement needs *atomic* H, produced when H₂ chemisorbs on bare iron. Cation‑exchanged sites (Ca²⁺, Ba²⁺, Cs⁺) and a fully silica‑terminated pore wall present no metallic dissociation sites at all, so the film is chemically incapable of making the atomic hydrogen the steel absorbs. A co‑blended Pt/Pd‑cluster zone deliberately does the opposite on the *outer* face: any H that does enter the wall is recombined back to H₂ and released harmlessly, so the layer acts as a hydrogen "one‑way exit."
- **It removes the accelerants.** The same pores getter the trace H₂S, CO₂, moisture and mercaptan odorant that dramatically worsen hydrogen uptake (H₂S is a classic recombination poison that forces H into the metal) and cause internal corrosion pitting — the pits that nucleate hydrogen cracks in the first place.
- **Self‑diagnosing.** The film's dielectric constant tracks its hydrogen and water loading, so a simple electrode ring at each pig‑launcher station reports the *actual* hydrogen flux reaching the wall — a direct, auditable measure of remaining pipeline life, replacing today's fracture‑mechanics estimates and periodic in‑line inspection guesswork. A thermal‑desorption ramp on a coupon gives a forensic history of what the line has been carrying.
- **Applied and repaired in place.** The coating is deposited from a cheap silica/alumina/soda sol pigged through the existing line at <200 °C — no excavation, no re‑pipe — and damaged patches are re‑grown by the same chemistry. Being an inorganic mineral, it is non‑flammable, radiation‑hard, and immune to the UV, solvent and thermal ageing that ends the life of polymer liners.

**Applications:** repurposing hundreds of thousands of kilometres of existing natural‑gas transmission and distribution steel for 100 % hydrogen; salt‑cavern and vessel storage; hydrogen compressors, valves and refuelling hardware at 350–700 bar; H₂‑burning gas‑turbine and engine components; ammonia‑cracker and refinery hydrogen service; and, in the same chemistry, protection of high‑strength fasteners, drill strings and subsea hardware from cathodic‑protection hydrogen charging — turning the hydrogen economy's most expensive metallurgical problem into a mineral skin sprayed on the inside of steel that already exists.

**Zeolite "pheromone metronome" — a temperature‑compensated mating‑disruption dispenser that protects orchards and forests for a whole season from a single hanging pellet.**

Mating disruption (flooding a crop with synthetic sex pheromone so males cannot find females) is the cleanest pest control that exists — no insecticide, no residue, no resistance, no harm to bees or predators. It fails commercially for one reason: **release rate physics**. Today's rubber septa, polymer ropes and membrane sachets emit pheromone in proportion to its vapour pressure, which roughly doubles every 10 °C. So a dispenser dumps most of its load during the first hot week, drops below the disruption threshold by mid‑flight, and the labile conjugated‑diene acetates and aldehydes that most moths use are simultaneously destroyed by UV and atmospheric oxidation. Growers must re‑hang dispensers two or three times a season, which is why the technique is confined to high‑value crops.

**The invention:** a thumbnail‑sized pellet or twist‑tie clip made of a shaped, dust‑free laminate of high‑silica frameworks (dealuminated Beta, mordenite, ZSM‑5, plus a cation‑exchanged CHA zone), vapour‑loaded with the target pheromone one molecule per cage.

- **Zero‑order, temperature‑compensated emission.** Release is not evaporation from a surface but *desorption from a pore*, governed by an adsorption isotherm rather than by Raoult's law. Choosing a framework whose adsorption enthalpy nearly cancels the compound's enthalpy of vaporisation flattens the temperature dependence: the pellet emits a near‑constant nanogram‑per‑hour plume from a cold spring night to a 40 °C afternoon, instead of a spike‑then‑nothing curve. Loading, pore aperture and Si/Al ratio set the rate, so "8 weeks of codling moth" becomes a specification rather than a hope — and a blend of two frameworks gives a deliberate ramp that tracks the pest's flight phenology.
- **The molecule survives the season.** Sealed one‑per‑cage inside a rigid mineral, the pheromone cannot dimerise, isomerise (E/Z scrambling ruins most commercial blends) or be reached by ozone, UV or singlet oxygen — the degradation that quietly halves the efficacy of every polymer dispenser. Multi‑component blends stay in their correct ratio, which is what the insect actually recognises.
- **Blend fidelity by pore selection.** In a polymer matrix the lighter component of a two‑ or three‑component blend evaporates first, so the emitted ratio drifts away from the biologically active one. Here each component can be housed in its own framework, tuned so that all of them leave at the ratio the female emits, for the whole season.
- **Attract‑and‑kill and monitoring from the same platform.** A Cu²⁺/Zn²⁺‑exchanged zone can co‑release a trace insecticide or an entomopathogenic spore only at the pellet surface; and because pheromone remaining in the pores is read non‑destructively by weighing or a dielectric probe, a grower or an area‑wide programme knows exactly how much dispenser life is left and can prove deployment for organic certification and subsidy audits.
- **Rechargeable, inert, cheap.** Pellets are collected at season's end, baked clean and re‑soaked in pheromone vapour for many seasons; the spent mineral is inert clay‑grade aluminosilicate, not a plastic tie or a rubber septum left in the orchard floor. It is non‑flammable, unaffected by rain, sprinkler irrigation, dust or 50 °C storage, and needs no cold chain — which is exactly what defeats pheromone logistics in tropical agriculture today.

**Applications:** codling moth, oriental fruit moth and grape berry moth in orchards and vineyards; pink bollworm in cotton; fall armyworm, tuta absoluta and diamondback moth in smallholder vegetables; bark beetle and gypsy‑moth suppression across forests, where dispensers must be air‑dropped once and work unattended for months; stored‑product moth control in warehouses; and, inverted as an *attractant* cartridge, standardised, non‑degrading lures for pest‑monitoring trap networks — turning mating disruption from a high‑maintenance boutique technique into a single ceramic pellet hung once a year.

**Zeolite "un‑glue" — a debond‑on‑demand structural adhesive that lets bonded products be taken apart for repair and recycling.**

Blend 5–15 vol % of sub‑micron, high‑silica zeolite crystals (Beta/ZSM‑5/faujasite) into an epoxy, acrylic or polyurethane structural adhesive. Before mixing, the pores are vapour‑loaded with a guest — water, an alcohol, a low‑boiling ester or a blocked amine — held at 60–90 kJ/mol, and the crystal outer surface is silane‑coupled to the resin.

- **In service the particles are pure benefit.** The imprisoned guest cannot escape at room temperature, so it never plasticises the joint; meanwhile the *unfilled* fraction of the pore volume gets­ters the ingressing water, acids and hydrolysis products that cause bondline degradation — the dominant long‑term failure mode of every structural adhesive. The hard, well‑bonded crystals also act as crack‑pinning tougheners, raising fracture energy, and their low CTE reduces cure shrinkage and residual stress.
- **Debonding is a switch, not a fight.** Heat the joint to 150–220 °C — with a hot plate, an induction coil through the metal adherend, or (uniquely) a microwave pulse, since a *loaded* zeolite couples strongly to microwaves while the dry polymer does not — and every particle desorbs its guest simultaneously, **inside** the bondline. The released vapour generates local pressure at exactly the polymer–substrate interface, nucleates micro‑voids and chemically attacks the interfacial bonds, so the joint loses most of its shear strength in seconds and the parts lift apart cleanly, with no solvent bath, no grinding, no prying and no damage to either adherend. Because the trigger is a desorption step, it is sharp and tunable: framework and cation choice set the release temperature, so the "unlock" point can be placed safely above the product's service temperature.
- **Self‑limiting and self‑reporting.** Only the heated zone debonds, so a technician can release one component from an assembly; and the adhesive's dielectric constant tracks its guest and moisture loading, so a simple electrode gives a non‑destructive read of both remaining debond capacity and bondline health (water ingress) over the product's life.
- **Why zeolite rather than expandable thermoplastic microspheres or azo blowing agents:** the crystalline mineral is inert, non‑flammable, does not creep or soften, survives cure exotherms and decades of thermal cycling without leaking its payload, releases no decomposition products or toxic gases, and is *rechargeable* — recovered adhesive‑bearing parts can be re‑soaked in guest vapour, and the mineral itself is clay‑grade cheap.

**Applications:** cell‑to‑pack EV battery adhesives, which today make modules effectively unrecyclable and unrepairable; smartphone, laptop and appliance assembly, where glued‑in glass and batteries are the core of the "right to repair" fight; bonded aircraft and wind‑turbine composite structures needing field repair and end‑of‑life fibre recovery; automotive multi‑material joints that must be separated for steel/aluminium/CFRP recycling streams; and glazing, dental and orthopaedic cements — turning permanent adhesive bonding, the biggest obstacle to a circular economy in manufactured goods, into a joint that can be switched off with a pulse of heat.

**Zeolite "light‑writable paper" — inkless, rewritable printing in which the pigment is a silver cluster living inside the pores.**

Coat ordinary paper, board or a plastic sheet with a thin (2–10 µm) layer of Ag⁺‑exchanged, small‑pore zeolite crystals (Ag‑LTA/CHA/faujasite) bound in a clear binder.

- **Writing with light, not toner:** a low‑power UV or blue laser/LED array photo‑reduces the exchanged Ag⁺ in the illuminated pixels into few‑atom silver clusters trapped inside the cages. These clusters have enormous absorption cross‑sections and colour the layer intensely (yellow‑brown to near‑black, and — by tuning framework, cation co‑exchange and cluster nuclearity — into distinct luminescent colours for multi‑colour printing). No ink, no toner cartridge, no ribbon, no drum, no consumable of any kind.
- **Erasing with heat:** a 100–150 °C pass (a roller, a hot plate, or an IR flash) re‑oxidises and re‑disperses the clusters back onto their framework exchange sites, returning the sheet to white. Because the silver never leaves the crystal — it only changes its state of aggregation inside a 0.5 nm cage — the cycle is chemically closed and can be repeated hundreds to thousands of times. Nothing is added and nothing is consumed but a few joules per page.
- **Why zeolites beat existing rewritable media:** leuco‑dye/thermochromic papers fade in weeks, are erased by a hot car or a coffee cup, and yellow under UV; photochromic organics bleach out. Here the "pigment" is a metal cluster imprisoned in a rigid mineral: it is stable indefinitely in the dark, unaffected by humidity, solvents, abrasion or fire, and the sheet is written by light but erased only above a sharp, chosen temperature — set by framework and cation choice, so the erase point can be placed well above any ambient condition.
- **Free extra functions from the same coating:** the residual Ag⁺ makes the sheet antimicrobial (self‑sanitising menus, hospital charts, shared documents); the empty micropores getter moisture and VOCs, so the substrate is also its own archival buffer; a hidden framework/cation "molecular barcode" in the coating authenticates every sheet by handheld Raman; and because the written state is *latent luminescent* as well as absorbing, machine‑readable data can be printed invisibly under the human‑readable text.
- **Security mode:** a whole document can be wiped irreversibly and instantly by a single heat pulse — genuine one‑button destruction of a physical page — and, conversely, sensitive drafts can be printed on a medium that leaves no toner residue, no imaging drum image and no shredder waste.

**Applications:** office and label printing where >90 % of pages are read once and discarded (shipping labels, receipts, boarding passes, price tags, meeting handouts, exam papers, hospital wristbands and charts); reusable classroom worksheets and books for schools that cannot afford paper; digital signage and shelf‑edge labels that hold their image with zero power; secure and classified document handling; and packaging that is relabelled rather than reprinted — turning printing from a consumable‑driven, deforesting industry into writing and rewriting light onto a permanent sheet of mineral.

**Zeolite "oxygen depot" — injectable mineral crystals that re‑oxygenate tumours so radiotherapy actually works.**

Hypoxia is the oldest unsolved problem in cancer treatment: cells starved of oxygen are 2–3× more radioresistant (and resist photodynamic therapy and many chemotherapies) because the killing chemistry requires O₂ to "fix" radical damage to DNA. Breathing high‑pressure oxygen or dosing hypoxia‑activated prodrugs has repeatedly failed because oxygen never reaches the necrotic core.

**The invention:** ~100–200 nm crystals of a Co(II)‑ or Cu(I)‑exchanged large‑pore zeolite (faujasite‑Y / LTA), PEGylated and injected intratumorally, delivered by catheter, or embedded in the brachytherapy spacer/hydrogel already implanted before treatment. Before use the crystals are charged with oxygen at modest pressure: the exchanged cations bind O₂ *reversibly* as a coordination complex — the same chemistry that lets these sites pick oxygen out of air — so the particle carries orders of magnitude more oxygen per unit volume than a perfluorocarbon emulsion, as a dry, shelf‑stable powder rather than a fragile cold‑chain emulsion.

- **Release is governed by the tumour, not by a timer.** Binding follows an isotherm, so O₂ is given up fastest exactly where pO₂ is lowest — the hypoxic and necrotic zones — and essentially not at all in normoxic tissue. That is self‑titrating reoxygenation with no pump, no gas, no hyperbaric chamber, and none of the systemic hyperoxia toxicity of breathing 100 % O₂.
- **Rechargeable *in situ* between fractions.** Radiotherapy is given over 20–30 daily fractions; the same particles re‑load from the blood's own dissolved oxygen (or from a brief oxygen‑breathing session) between sessions, so one injection sensitises the whole course rather than a single dose.
- **The pores do a second job.** Co‑occluded payloads — a radiosensitiser (nimorazole‑type), a chemotherapeutic, or a STING/TLR agonist — are released by ion displacement driven by the acidic, high‑lactate tumour microenvironment, i.e. dosed only inside the tumour. Cation‑exchange sites simultaneously mop up the Fe²⁺/Cu²⁺ and buffer the H⁺ that make tumours acidic and immunosuppressive.
- **It is its own fiducial and dosimeter.** A Ba²⁺/Gd³⁺‑exchanged fraction makes the depot radiopaque and MRI‑bright, so the same injection is the image‑guidance fiducial marker radiotherapy already requires, and its oxygen loading is readable by ¹⁹F‑free MRI/EPR oximetry — giving, for the first time, a direct map of whether the tumour was actually oxygenated at the moment the beam was on.
- **Also the enabler for photodynamic and sonodynamic therapy**, both of which stall in hypoxic tissue because they consume the very oxygen they need.

**Why a zeolite:** the aluminosilicate is inert, non‑biodegradable and non‑metabolised, gamma‑ and heat‑sterilisable with indefinite shelf life at 45 °C (no cold chain), radiation‑hard so the beam itself does not degrade it, and every cation sits on a crystallographically identical site — so the oxygen release curve is a reproducible material constant rather than a batch‑to‑batch accident, and the metal cannot leach out of a cage smaller than its hydrated exit path.

**Applications:** hypoxia‑driven cancers where local control is poor — head and neck, cervix, glioblastoma, pancreas, soft‑tissue sarcoma; brachytherapy and stereotactic boosts; oxygen support for photodynamic therapy of skin and oesophageal tumours; and, in the same chemistry, an implantable oxygen depot for ischaemic wounds, skin flaps and transplanted islet or engineered‑tissue grafts, which die because nothing supplies oxygen before vessels grow in.

**Zeolite "colour star" — cation‑exchanged pyrotechnic grains that make fireworks, flares and signal rounds bright, pure‑coloured and non‑polluting.**

The idea: replace the metal‑salt colourants and the chlorine donor in pyrotechnic "stars" with ion‑exchanged zeolite microgranules — Sr²⁺ (red), Ba²⁺ (green), Cu²⁺ (blue), Na⁺ (yellow), Li⁺ (crimson) — one ion per crystallographic site, with a fuel/oxidiser (nitrate, or a nitro‑organic) occluded in the same pores.

- **Atomic dispersion = more light from less metal.** In a conventional star the colour comes from micron lumps of SrCO₃ or Ba(NO₃)₂ that must first melt and vaporise, so most of the metal never emits and much of the flame is grey‑body glow. Here every emitting cation is already isolated on a framework site, released as free atoms/monochlorides the instant the grain reaches flame temperature — brighter, more saturated, more reproducible colour at a fraction of the metal loading, with far less unburnt metal falling out over the crowd and into lakes and reservoirs.
- **No perchlorate, no chlorine donor.** Because oxidiser and fuel are held *inside* the pore, in molecular contact with the emitter, combustion is fast and complete without ammonium/potassium perchlorate; and the pore's confinement stabilises the copper emitter well enough to give a true blue without PVC/Parlon chlorine donors — removing at a stroke the perchlorate that contaminates groundwater and thyroid function, and the chlorinated‑dioxin and HCl emissions that are closing displays in Europe.
- **Colour as a timed sequence, not a layer.** Framework choice and cation exchange set each grain's release temperature, so a single blended star can be programmed to change colour, or to hold a colour, purely by mineral formulation rather than by the laborious multi‑layer rolling used today.
- **Safe to make, ship and store.** The reactive metal is ion‑exchanged into a mineral rather than present as a hygroscopic, friction‑sensitive salt: the grains are non‑caking in humid tropical storage (the reason so many stocks are scrapped), far less friction/impact sensitive during pressing, and inert if the device fails to fire — a dud is a lump of clay, not a live oxidiser.
- **Bonus formats.** The same chemistry gives long‑shelf‑life marine distress and rescue flares that work after years in a damp locker; agricultural bird‑scaring and avalanche rounds with no heavy‑metal residue on crops or snowpack; and, with Cs⁺/Rb⁺ or IR‑emitting exchange, spectrally tailored decoy flares and calibration sources.

**Application:** low‑emission public firework displays, indoor/close‑proximity pyrotechnics, marine and aviation signal flares, and military countermeasure flares — turning the most polluting piece of celebration technology into a grain of exchanged mineral that burns cleanly and emits colour atom by atom.

**Zeolite "anaerobic blood bag" — a sachet of mineral inside the pack that lets red cells be stored oxygen‑free, doubling usable shelf life.**

Stored red cells deteriorate ("storage lesion") mainly through oxidative damage: residual O₂ in the bag oxidises haemoglobin and membrane lipids, ATP and 2,3‑DPG collapse, cells stiffen and haemolyse, so units are discarded at 42 days and transfused blood delivers oxygen poorly for the first day. Anaerobic storage fixes this, but today it needs bulky external scavenger canisters and gas‑impermeable overwraps.

**The device:** a small, welded‑in sachet (or a coating on the inner wall of the bag) containing a laminate of tailored zeolites, sealed with the unit at collection.

- **Oxygen stripped and held:** Co(II)/Cu(I)‑exchanged faujasite/LTA binds O₂ reversibly on isolated cation sites, pulling dissolved and headspace oxygen down to near zero within hours at 4 °C — no hydrogen, no reactive iron powder, no exothermic chemistry next to a blood product.
- **CO₂ clamped, not removed entirely:** a Ca‑exchanged chabassite zone buffers the CO₂ that acidifies the unit and destroys 2,3‑DPG, holding pH on a plateau so rejuvenation solutions become unnecessary.
- **Plasticiser and degradation products gettered:** a hydrophobic high‑silica layer adsorbs the DEHP leaching from the PVC bag and the aldehydes/peroxides generated by lipid oxidation — the molecules implicated in transfusion‑related inflammation.
- **Self‑reporting:** the sachet's dielectric constant/colour indicator reads its O₂ loading through the bag wall, giving a per‑unit, non‑destructive proof that anaerobic conditions were maintained the whole time — something no current storage system can show.
- **Why zeolite:** inert, gamma‑ and steam‑sterilisable, endotoxin‑free, sheds no fibres or leachables into a parenteral product, indefinitely shelf‑stable at tropical temperatures, and clay‑grade cheap; each cation sits on a crystallographically identical site, so the oxygen‑binding curve is a reproducible material constant.

**Applications:** extending red‑cell shelf life to 8–10 weeks and improving post‑transfusion oxygen delivery in routine hospital banking; reducing wastage in blood services that currently discard a significant fraction of donations; enabling blood stockpiles for rural, military, maritime and disaster settings where resupply is slow; and the same sachet chemistry in platelet, plasma and organ‑perfusion bags — turning the storage lesion into a problem solved by a pebble of mineral sitting in the bag.

**Zeolite "contrail cutter" — a jet‑exhaust cartridge that dries the plume so it cannot form a contrail.**

Contrail cirrus causes roughly as much warming as all the CO₂ aviation has ever emitted, and it needs only two ingredients: exhaust water vapour (~1.25 kg per kg of fuel) and soot particles to seed the ice. Remove either and the plume vanishes.

The device is a lightweight, low‑back‑pressure zeolite honeycomb in a slipstream duct tapping the cooled core exhaust (or the whole flow of a hydrogen/SAF engine, whose water‑rich plume is especially contrail‑prone):

- **Soot gate:** a hydrophobic high‑silica (Beta/ZSM‑5) front layer with Pt/Pd clusters grown inside its cages adsorbs the semi‑volatile organics coating soot and oxidises the fine carbon at exhaust temperature — removing the ice nuclei themselves.
- **Water sink:** a hydrophilic Na‑A/SAPO core, cold‑soaked by −50 °C ram air, adsorbs the exhaust water and drops the plume's vapour partial pressure below the Schmidt–Appleman threshold, so ice supersaturation is never reached. The adsorption enthalpy (~3–4 MJ per kg of water) is dumped into the bypass, slightly re‑heating the plume — which further suppresses ice formation.
- **Selective operation:** only ~5–10 % of flights, crossing thin ice‑supersaturated layers, produce almost all persistent contrails, so a valve switches the cartridge in for minutes rather than hours, paying the mass/drag penalty only when it matters.
- **Discharge and reuse:** descending into warm, dry air purges the bed; the water is vented harmlessly or condensed into a tank as potable cabin water, ballast, or feed for a fuel‑cell APU. The mineral cycles indefinitely.
- **Why zeolite:** stable past 800 °C, vibration‑ and sulfur‑tolerant, non‑flammable, sheds nothing into the engine, and because desorption is stoichiometric the water removed per flight is a directly auditable measure of contrail forcing avoided — the verification that contrail‑avoidance carbon credits currently lack.

**Application:** the fastest, cheapest lever on aviation's non‑CO₂ climate impact — retrofit ducts for long‑haul jets on contrail‑prone corridors, and a design‑in requirement for hydrogen aircraft, whose plumes would otherwise contrail almost everywhere.

**Zeolite "fryer keeper" — a regenerable in‑line cartridge that keeps deep‑frying oil food‑safe indefinitely, instead of dumping it every few days.**

Commercial fryers discard oil not because the triglycerides are gone but because four things accumulate: water from the food (driving hydrolysis), free fatty acids and polar oxidation products, the polymerised gums that darken oil and glaze the vat, and the aldehydes/acrolein that create the fumes, off‑flavour and the acrylamide/HNE toxicology problem. Paper "oil filters" only catch crumbs. The invention is a swappable ceramic cartridge in the fryer's recirculation loop, built as a laminate:

- **3 Å LTA zone:** windows admit water (2.65 Å) but exclude every triglyceride and every flavour molecule, so the oil is dried below the hydrolysis threshold *without* stripping it — the root cause of rising free fatty acid and falling smoke point is removed continuously rather than diluted by topping up.
- **Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺‑exchanged wide‑pore Y/Beta zone:** basic cation sites neutralise and hold the free fatty acids, aldehydes, acrolein and polar oxidation products, keeping Total Polar Materials (the legal condemnation limit in most of Europe) flat instead of climbing, and cutting the fume that makes kitchen air a recognised occupational carcinogen.
- **Hydrophobic high‑silica zone:** size‑selectively adsorbs the small, dark, bitter degradation and Maillard fragments and the fish/onion flavour carry‑over between batches, while the bulky triglycerides and added antioxidants are excluded and pass straight through — so one vat can cook fish and doughnuts without cross‑tainting.
- **Occluded antioxidant re‑dosing:** a fourth zone is pre‑loaded with tocopherol/rosemary extract, displaced from the pores by the very peroxides that signal antioxidant depletion — the oil is re‑stabilised on demand, in proportion to how hard the fryer is working.
- **Regeneration and a built‑in logbook:** a 300–400 °C air burn‑off (a bench oven, or the fryer's own boil‑out cycle) empties and de‑cokes the cartridge for hundreds of cycles. Because each species desorbs at its own temperature, the regeneration ramp yields a desorption spectrum — an auditable record of exactly how much water, acid and polar material the kitchen generated, replacing today's guesswork test strips.
- **Why zeolite:** separation by molecular size and polarity (unlike magnesium‑silicate and bleaching‑clay powders, which strip antioxidants and leave fines in the food), food‑grade, non‑flammable, stable at 190 °C, sheds nothing into the oil, and clay‑grade cheap.

**Application:** cutting the frying oil consumption of restaurants, fast‑food chains, snack plants and institutional kitchens by several‑fold — reducing the palm/soy demand and the used‑cooking‑oil waste stream, holding food quality and acrylamide/aldehyde exposure constant to the last portion, and letting off‑grid and remote kitchens (ships, camps, rural vendors) keep frying safely without a fresh‑oil supply chain.

**Zeolite "seizure sink" — a passive cortical implant that soaks up the ion surge that starts an epileptic seizure.**

Focal seizures begin as a local electrochemical failure: extracellular K⁺ climbs from ~3 mM toward 10–12 mM, depolarising neighbouring neurones, while glutamate floods the synaptic space and recruits the surrounding cortex. Drugs must be dosed systemically (sedation, teratogenicity, 30 % of patients refractory), and the alternatives are resective surgery or an implanted stimulator with a battery.

**The device:** a thin (100–300 µm), flexible mesh or hydrogel patch laid on the epileptogenic cortex (or a stereotactically injected slurry of 1–5 µm grains for deep foci), built from Na⁺/Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺-form clinoptilolite and LTA crystals bound in a soft, permeable silicone-hydrogel matrix.

- **Peak-shaving by ion exchange, not by a drug.** The framework's cages strongly prefer the large, weakly hydrated K⁺ over the huge Na⁺ background of interstitial fluid. Because uptake follows an isotherm, the patch absorbs K⁺ *fastest exactly when local K⁺ is highest* — during the pre-ictal surge — and gives it back as concentrations fall between events. It is a chemical capacitor that clips the peak without disturbing baseline neuronal firing, which is what makes it different from a drug or a lesion.
- **Glutamate and ammonium too.** Ca²⁺/La³⁺ sites bind the carboxylates of glutamate and aspartate, and a co-blended hydrophobic mesoporous fraction adsorbs them and the arachidonic-acid/inflammatory mediators of the ictal cascade; clinoptilolite sites strip NH₄⁺, the trigger in hepatic and metabolic seizures.
- **The counter-ion it gives back is itself an anticonvulsant.** Exchange is stoichiometric, so every K⁺ captured releases Mg²⁺/Ca²⁺ — Mg²⁺ blocks the NMDA receptor and Ca²⁺ raises the seizure threshold. The therapy is delivered by the same event that triggers it, with no pump, no battery, no electrode and no systemic dose.
- **Self-regenerating and unpowered.** Nothing is consumed: cerebrospinal and interstitial fluid re-load the sites with Na⁺/Ca²⁺ between seizures, so the implant works for years with no stimulation, no charging and no drug reservoir.
- **Why a zeolite:** an inert, non-degrading, non-swelling aluminosilicate — MRI-artefact-free and non-magnetic (unlike a stimulator), gamma-sterilisable, indefinitely shelf-stable with no cold chain, and it releases no organic degradation products into brain tissue.
- **It also records.** Explanted or sampled grains hold a stoichiometric record of how much K⁺ and glutamate they intercepted — an objective map of where and how hard the focus has been discharging, which today can only be inferred from EEG.

**Applications:** drug-resistant focal epilepsy, as a low-risk alternative to resection or responsive neurostimulation; peri-lesional prophylaxis after tumour or vascular neurosurgery; and, in the same chemistry, suppression of the spreading depolarisations that expand the damage zone in traumatic brain injury, ischaemic stroke penumbra and subarachnoid haemorrhage — turning seizure control from a systemic drug or an implanted computer into a passive patch of mineral that simply drinks the ions.

**Zeolite "water architect" cartridge — a programmable ion‑exchange puck that doesn't just soften water, it *writes* a specified mineral profile into it.**

A small food‑grade cartridge (in‑line on an espresso machine, kettle, tea urn, brewhouse liquor line, steam oven, dishwasher or ice machine) packed with a stack of clinoptilolite/LTA zeolite zones, each pre‑loaded by ion exchange with a different cation in a fixed stoichiometric ratio — Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, K⁺, Na⁺ — behind a high‑silica hydrophobic guard layer.

- **Take out what ruins the machine.** The first zone exchanges the incoming hardness and bicarbonate‑paired cations into the cages, so nothing precipitates as limescale on the boiler element or group head — the single commonest failure of every hot‑water appliance, and the reason commercial kitchens replace resin filters monthly.
- **Put back exactly what the drink needs.** Extraction chemistry is not "soft water good": coffee and tea need Mg²⁺ (which chelates the flavour acids), a little Ca²⁺ for body, and a controlled bicarbonate buffer; brewers need a defined sulfate:chloride ratio for hop bite versus malt roundness. Because zeolite exchange is stoichiometric, the downstream zones release cations in a *precisely metered* ratio as the incoming ions load the bed — so the cartridge outputs a target water recipe ("SCA brewing water", "Burton ale liquor", "Pilsen soft") rather than just stripped, flat, corrosive softened water.
- **The guard layer cleans the rest.** Hydrophobic high‑silica pores strip chlorine/chloramine, geosmin and earthy off‑flavours, pesticide and pharmaceutical residues, and a Ag⁺/Cu²⁺ rim stops the biofilm that makes filter housings a hygiene problem.
- **It reports and recharges itself.** A conductivity pair across the cartridge meters exactly how many equivalents have been exchanged, so it says when it is spent instead of relying on a litre counter; and it is regenerated by a simple brine or "recipe salt" soak, hundreds of times, instead of being thrown away like a resin‑and‑carbon pod.

**Application:** consistent, reproducible espresso, tea and beer from any municipal supply worldwide (the biggest uncontrolled variable in café and brewery quality), plus scale‑free, maintenance‑free hot‑water equipment — turning water treatment from "remove minerals and hope" into a printable ion recipe held inside a reusable rock.

**Zeolite "dry‑skin patch" antiperspirant — an aluminium‑free deodorant that stops sweat odour by adsorbing the sweat instead of plugging the gland.**

Today's antiperspirants work by pouring aluminium chlorohydrate into the duct so it gels and physically blocks the sweat gland — the mechanism behind irritation, fabric‑yellowing, and the (contested but commercially decisive) consumer fear about aluminium. "Natural" alternatives just add fragrance and baking soda, and fail within hours.

**The product:** a roll‑on/stick/patch in which the active is a blend of micron‑sized, food‑grade zeolite crystals — a hydrophilic Na‑A/SAPO fraction with a *steep, stepped* water isotherm, a hydrophobic high‑silica Beta/ZSM‑5 fraction, and a Zn²⁺/Cu²⁺‑exchanged clinoptilolite fraction — in a light silicone or emollient base.

- **Dryness without blocking a duct.** The stepped isotherm means the hydrophilic crystals hold essentially nothing at normal skin humidity, then switch on sharply the moment the microclimate saturates: they drink the sweat film as it appears (0.2–0.3 g water per gram), and give it straight back when the skin dries out. The gland keeps working normally — thermoregulation is untouched — but the skin surface never stays wet, which is what causes maceration, chafing and the damp‑shirt problem.
- **Odour removed, not perfumed.** Fresh sweat is odourless; the smell is bacterial cleavage of it into thioalcohols, short‑chain and branched fatty acids (3‑methyl‑2‑hexenoic acid) and ammonia. The hydrophobic pores physisorb exactly these small, volatile molecules, while the cation‑exchange sites capture the NH₄⁺ — so the odorant is taken out of the air rather than masked.
- **Bacteria dosed only where they are winning.** *Corynebacterium* and *Staphylococcus* metabolism acidifies the local surface; that H⁺ flux is what drives cation exchange, so Zn²⁺ is released precisely at the colonised, smelly patch and stops when the skin returns to its normal pH — an antimicrobial that self‑titrates, doesn't sterilise the whole skin microbiome, and doesn't select for resistance. Exchange also buffers the skin back toward its healthy acid mantle.
- **Why a zeolite:** it is an inert, non‑absorbed, already food/cosmetic‑grade mineral — no aluminium salt, no alcohol sting, no parabens, tasteless and odourless, non‑flammable, stable for years in tropical heat, and it leaves no acid‑and‑aluminium residue, which is the chemistry that actually yellows and rots shirt armpits. It is also self‑recharging: washing and drying (or simply a dry day) empties the pores completely, so the same crystals work indefinitely.
- **Extra formats from the same powder:** a wearable adhesive patch for hyperhidrosis and for people who cannot use aluminium (post‑mastectomy, dermatitis, radiotherapy fields); a shoe/insole and helmet‑liner dust; a dry powder for bed‑bound and incontinent patients where skin maceration precedes pressure sores; and a "sweat‑capture" version whose loaded crystals can be thermally desorbed into a GC‑MS, giving a non‑invasive record of drugs, metabolites, electrolyte loss and hydration status from an ordinary day's wear.

**Application:** an effective, genuinely aluminium‑free personal antiperspirant/deodorant, plus clinical hyperhidrosis and skin‑maceration management — turning odour control from "block the gland and hide the smell" into "adsorb the water, adsorb the odorant, and medicate only the bacteria that are actually causing it," using nothing but a pinch of mineral.

**Zeolite "quake foam" — injectable mineral grains that hold a permanent bubble in their pores and make loose ground liquefaction‑proof.**

**The problem:** liquefaction destroys ports, levees, tailings dams and whole city blocks (Niigata, Christchurch, Palu). Loose saturated sand tries to contract during shaking, water cannot escape fast enough, pore pressure climbs to the overburden stress, effective stress falls to zero and the ground flows. Geotechnical engineers know the cheapest fix: *induced partial saturation* — a few percent of gas in the pore fluid makes the fluid compressible and can double or triple liquefaction resistance. It is almost never used, because free bubbles dissolve, coalesce and migrate away within months to years, and nobody can prove they are still there.

**The invention:** permeation‑grout the liquefiable layer with a dilute slurry of 0.1–0.5 mm sintered zeolite microgranules (chabazite/clinoptilolite/high‑silica CHA composite) whose micropores have been pre‑charged with a sparingly soluble gas (N₂ or Ar) at modest pressure.

- **A bubble that cannot dissolve.** The gas is not a free bubble subject to Laplace pressure and Ostwald ripening; it is *adsorbed* in 3–4 Å cages at 15–25 kJ/mol. It therefore has no driving force to dissolve into the groundwater and no interface to coalesce across, yet it still delivers exactly what partial saturation needs: a distributed, highly compressible phase inside the pore fluid. Each grain is a permanent micro‑airbag with a design life of decades rather than months.
- **Pressure‑spike buffering.** When shaking drives the pore pressure up, water is pushed into the grain's meso/macropore network and further compresses/displaces the held gas; when the cycle reverses, the gas expands and water is expelled. The soil's fluid stiffness is cut by orders of magnitude, so excess pore pressure never reaches the effective‑stress ceiling — the mechanism is a distributed hydraulic accumulator rather than a stiffening or densifying treatment.
- **Drainage and dilatancy for free.** The hard, angular, macroporous grains also act as micro‑drains, shortening drainage paths, and their rough surfaces raise the sand's dilatancy and interparticle friction; a lime‑ or silicate‑activated fraction reacts pozzolanically with the framework's own reactive alumina to add light, permanent cohesion without turning the soil into an impermeable block.
- **It can be verified, which is what regulators actually need.** Gas content changes the soil's P‑wave velocity, resistivity and dielectric constant, so a cheap cross‑hole or embedded‑electrode survey reports the *remaining* liquefaction resistance at any time in the structure's life — the auditable proof that no bubble‑injection or biogas (denitrification) method can give.
- **Recharge instead of re‑build.** If capacity ever falls, the same injection wells are used to re‑pressurise the grains with gas; nothing has been consumed. And because the framework's exchange sites simultaneously grab ammonium, heavy metals and radium, treating contaminated fill or tailings improves the groundwater at the same time.
- **Why zeolite specifically:** clay‑grade cost at the enormous volumes ground improvement demands; a crystalline aluminosilicate that cannot rot, creep, biodegrade or be eaten by bacteria over a 100‑year design life; chemically inert in saline and acidic groundwater; and low enough viscosity as a dilute slurry to be permeation‑grouted through small‑diameter directional holes **underneath existing buildings** — which is the whole point, since the world's liquefiable ground is mostly already built on and cannot be dug up, vibro‑compacted or jet‑grouted.

**Application:** seismic retrofit of existing city blocks, hospitals and schools on reclaimed land; quay walls, airport runways and buried lifelines (the assets whose liquefaction failure paralyses post‑earthquake recovery); levees and river dykes; bridge and viaduct foundations; and — the largest prize — upstream tailings dams, whose dominant collapse mode is static or seismic liquefaction of the deposited slimes. It turns liquefaction mitigation from mass excavation and densification into an injection of mineral grains, each carrying a bubble that can never escape.

**Zeolite "comet catcher" — a passive volatile-capture canister that lets sample-return missions bring back a planet's *gases*, not just its dust.**

Every sample-return mission so far (Stardust, Hayabusa, OSIRIS-REx) brings home rock and grain, and loses the scientifically most valuable part — the volatiles (H₂O, CO₂, CO, CH₄, NH₃, N₂, noble gases, HCN and complex organics) — because they boil off during collection, cruise and re-entry heating, and because carrying a cryogenic cold trap costs mass, power and reliability no small spacecraft can spare.

**The device:** a small, valved ceramic canister packed with a stacked laminate of frameworks, each matched to one volatile class, mounted on the sampling head or the atmospheric inlet.

- **Cold capture with no cryocooler.** In the shade of the sampling arm the canister radiates to ~100–150 K, and at those temperatures a hydrophilic Na-X/chabazite layer swallows H₂O, CO₂, NH₃ and HCN, a high-silica hydrophobic layer holds CH₄ and the organics, and an Ag⁺/Ba²⁺-exchanged small-pore "trapdoor" layer (LTA/RHO) mechanically encapsulates Ar, Kr and Xe when the cages cool. The pumping is done by chemistry, not by a compressor, a valve train or a pressure vessel.
- **The molecules are held, not merely stored.** Guests sit at 30–100 kJ/mol in rigid cages, so the sample survives months of cruise, a warm-up to +40 °C, and the re-entry thermal pulse without venting — the failure mode that has forced every previous mission to treat its volatiles as expendable. Nothing is under pressure, so a hard landing releases nothing.
- **Isotopes and fragile species preserved.** Because the sample is immobilised on identical crystallographic sites rather than condensed as a frost that can sublime, fractionate or re-react, the D/H, ¹⁵N/¹⁴N and noble-gas isotope ratios — the fingerprints used to test whether comets delivered Earth's oceans — are locked in as collected, and amino acids and other prebiotic organics are shielded from UV, radiation and oxidation inside the pores.
- **Readout is a temperature ramp.** In the receiving laboratory a slow thermal-desorption ramp into a mass spectrometer releases each species at its own characteristic temperature, so the canister behaves as a self-separating chromatographic archive: a full inventory of what was captured, when (by layer position along the diffusion path), and in what ratio.
- **Same hardware, other duties.** Run on the intake of an atmospheric probe it collects and concentrates trace species from Mars, Titan or Venus for return or in-situ analysis; on a lander it samples an outgassing plume or a drill hole; and, warmed on demand, it becomes a clean gas source for onboard instrument calibration.

**Why zeolites:** an inorganic, radiation-hard, non-outgassing mineral that is unaffected by vacuum, dust, vibration and 800 °C sterilisation (so it passes planetary-protection bake-out that would destroy any polymer sorbent), it is regenerable and re-usable for ground testing, and it weighs grams where a cryotrap weighs kilograms.

**Application:** turning comet, asteroid, lunar cold-trap, Enceladus-plume and Mars sample-return missions from "we brought back rocks" into "we brought back the ices and the atmosphere too" — the measurements that decide where Earth's water and organics came from — using nothing but a valved brick of mineral.

**Zeolite "chemo sink" — a deployable intravascular cartridge that catches chemotherapy drug *after* it has passed through the tumour, so the dose can be raised without the side effects.**

In trans‑arterial chemoembolisation of liver, kidney or limb tumours, only a fraction of the injected drug stays in the target; the rest washes straight into the systemic circulation within minutes and causes the cardiotoxicity, marrow suppression, hair loss, nausea and neuropathy that cap the dose — and therefore cap the cure rate. The invention is a small, catheter‑delivered mesh "umbrella" coated with a drug‑selective zeolite, opened in the vein *downstream* of the tumour for the twenty minutes of the infusion, then collapsed and withdrawn.

- **Selective capture by cage chemistry:** the coating is a hierarchical, cation‑exchanged zeolite (dealuminated Beta/faujasite with grafted 10–50 nm transport mesopores over a micropore core). Ca²⁺/La³⁺/Zn²⁺ sites bind the protonated amine of doxorubicin and the carboxylate/platinum aqua species of cisplatin and oxaliplatin electrostatically, while the pore mouth size‑excludes albumin, immunoglobulins and clotting factors, which pass through untouched. Binding constants are high enough to strip 70–90 % of the drug in a single pass at physiological flow, in the first pass — before the drug has ever seen a heart cell.
- **Tumour dose *up*, body dose *down*:** because the systemic tail is removed rather than the tumour dose reduced, interventional radiologists can inject 2–5× the current drug load into the feeding artery, which is exactly the regime where response rates rise steeply — a "one‑way valve" for cytotoxic chemistry.
- **A blood‑contacting mineral that behaves:** the crystals are skinned with a heparinised/zwitterionic layer so platelets never touch the aluminosilicate; the framework itself is non‑swelling, sheds no polymer fines or leachable ligand, and is gamma‑ and steam‑sterilisable with indefinite shelf life at 45 °C — no cold chain, clay‑grade cost, ideal for a single‑use disposable in low‑resource oncology.
- **It measures its own benefit:** eluting the retrieved device and reading the desorbed drug gives a direct, per‑patient milligram figure for how much cytotoxic actually escaped the tumour — the pharmacokinetic number oncologists currently have to model from blood sampling. Different exchanged cations swap the same platform between anthracyclines, platinums, and radioembolisation escape (unbound ⁹⁰Y microsphere leachate).

**Applications:** liver‑directed chemoembolisation of hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal metastases; isolated limb and pelvic perfusion for sarcoma and melanoma; intra‑arterial chemotherapy for retinoblastoma and head‑and‑neck tumours (where a child's eye is treated but the marrow pays for it); and, in a larger extracorporeal format, a post‑infusion "rinse" filter that shortens the toxic tail of ordinary intravenous chemotherapy — turning the dose‑limiting toxicity of cancer treatment into something filtered out of the bloodstream by a folded umbrella of mineral.

**Zeolite "smart tread" — a caged‑antiozonant tyre filler that stops 6PPD‑quinone reaching salmon streams, and doses the rubber's protection only where it is attacked.**

Replace part of the silica/carbon‑black filler in tyre tread and sidewall compound with silane‑coupled, sub‑micron high‑silica zeolite crystals (Beta/ZSM‑5/faujasite) whose pores have been vapour‑loaded with the antiozonant and antioxidant package (6PPD‑type amines, waxes, phenolics) one molecule per cage, plus a cation‑exchanged (Ca²⁺/Zn²⁺) fraction.

- **The problem it solves:** every tyre must contain an antiozonant that continuously blooms to the surface to stop ozone cracking. That same bloom washes off in rain, and its ozone‑reaction product 6PPD‑quinone is acutely lethal to coho salmon and other aquatic life at nanogram‑per‑litre levels — now the single largest emerging regulatory threat to the tyre industry, with no drop‑in replacement chemistry available.
- **Dosing by attack, not by diffusion:** the amine is held in the pores at 60–90 kJ/mol, so it cannot bloom, sweat out or be rinsed off during storage or driving. It is displaced only by the ozone‑ and heat‑driven acidic degradation products generated at a *cracking* surface — so protection is delivered exactly where and when the rubber is being oxidised, at a fraction of today's loading, and essentially none is exported to the road.
- **The pores catch the product as well as the precursor:** unfilled channels and Ca²⁺/Zn²⁺ exchange sites in the outer wear layer adsorb 6PPD‑quinone, the nitrosamines and the PAH/zinc leachate as they form, so tyre‑wear particles shed onto the road arrive as inert, largely detoxified mineral‑bound debris rather than a soluble aquatic poison.
- **Mechanical bonus, not a penalty:** the hard, silane‑bonded crystalline filler reinforces like precipitated silica but with a rigid internal pore volume, giving lower hysteresis (rolling‑resistance/fuel saving) at equal wet grip, while the same micropores buffer the water and heat that drive belt‑edge and inner‑liner ageing.
- **Auditable and recyclable:** because each guest desorbs at its own temperature, a thermal‑desorption ramp on a tread coupon gives a direct measure of remaining antiozonant life (a real tyre‑ageing test, replacing calendar age limits); and in pyrolytic tyre recycling the mineral survives and is recovered as reusable filler.

**Application:** compliance‑ready tread compounds for road tyres, plus the same filler in conveyor belts, seals, hoses and marine fenders — turning the most ecologically damaging molecule in rubber chemistry into one imprisoned in a grain of mineral and released only at the crack it is meant to heal.

**Zeolite "mineral‑seasoned timber" — a wood impregnation that makes untreated softwood rot‑proof, termite‑proof, dimensionally stable and fire‑resistant, without leaching biocides.**

Vacuum‑pressure impregnate sawn timber, poles, sleepers or CLT laminae with a dilute aqueous slurry of sub‑micron zeolite crystals (Cu²⁺/Zn²⁺‑exchanged clinoptilolite and LTA, blended with a stepped‑isotherm SAPO and a hydrophobic silicalite fraction), which deposit inside the lumens, pits and cell walls and are then dried in place.

- **Moisture clamped below the decay threshold.** Wood only rots above ~20 % moisture content. The stepped water isotherm makes the mineral a *buffer*, not a desiccant: it absorbs the surge from rain, dew or a plumbing leak and gives it back when the air dries, pinning the timber on a plateau. Fungi and mould never get the water activity they need, and the same buffering removes most of the seasonal swelling, cupping, checking and glue‑line stress that ages joinery, decking and mass‑timber panels.
- **Biocide dosed only where something is eating the wood.** Brown‑ and white‑rot fungi attack by secreting oxalic acid; termites likewise acidify their gut‑lined galleries. That H⁺ flux is exactly what drives cation exchange, so Cu²⁺/Zn²⁺ (and pore‑occluded borate, which normally leaches out of treated wood within a season) is released *at the infection front and nowhere else*, then stops. Leaching into soil and water — the reason CCA, creosote and copper azole are being restricted — collapses by orders of magnitude, and the treatment is recharged by a simple surface soak rather than by replacing the member.
- **Fire performance from the same grain.** Water held in the pores desorbs endothermically above ~120 °C (~3–4 MJ per kg), pinning the char front and delaying ignition, while a phosphate‑exchanged fraction is released only at that temperature to promote char rather than flame — an intumescent action built into the wood instead of painted on, and one that re‑arms itself from ambient humidity.
- **Bonus functions.** Hydrophobic pores adsorb the formaldehyde and VOCs off‑gassed by adhesives in engineered wood; UV‑absorbing exchanged cations slow surface greying; and because exchange is stoichiometric, a handheld XRF/conductivity reading on a core sample reports exactly how much biocide capacity and moisture buffering a 40‑year‑old member has left — condition assessment that currently requires destructive testing.

**Application:** rot‑ and termite‑resistant mass‑timber (CLT/glulam) construction, utility poles, railway sleepers, marine and agricultural structures, decking, cladding and fence posts — replacing heavy‑metal and creosote preservatives with a non‑leaching, self‑dosing, fire‑buffering mineral that lets cheap, fast‑grown softwood be used where only tropical hardwood or steel works today.

**Zeolite "cold‑lay road" — a foaming, self‑rejuvenating additive that lets asphalt be mixed and laid warm, and then repairs its own ageing for decades.**

The idea: batch 0.3–0.5 wt % of the bitumen with a dual‑charged zeolite powder — hydrophilic Na‑A/Na‑X grains loaded to ~20 wt % adsorbed water, blended with hydrophobic high‑silica Beta/ZSM‑5 grains whose pores are vapour‑loaded with a maltene‑rich rejuvenator (bio‑oil, ester or naphthenic fraction) held at 60–90 kJ/mol.

- **Warm‑mix foaming:** in the pugmill at 120–130 °C the hydrophilic fraction desorbs its water slowly and continuously (not as one steam burst, as a salt hydrate would), micro‑foaming the binder so it coats aggregate at 30–40 °C below hot‑mix temperature. That cuts paving fuel, CO₂ and the bitumen‑fume/PAH exposure that is the paving crew's dominant occupational hazard, and it extends the haul distance and the cold‑weather paving season — the two things that limit road repair logistics.
- **High recycled content:** the same lubricating foam lets 60–80 % reclaimed asphalt pavement be blended without overheating and re‑oxidising the old binder, which is what caps RAP use today.
- **Ageing repaired on demand, for decades:** road failure is oxidative — the binder loses maltenes, stiffens and cracks. The rejuvenator sits sealed in hydrophobic pores, so it cannot bleed out and soften the fresh mat. It is displaced only by the carboxylic acids and ketones that oxidation itself generates, and desorbs preferentially at the hot, cracked, sun‑baked spots — so the pavement re‑softens exactly where and when it is embrittling, instead of being sprayed with a blanket fog‑seal every few years.
- **Self‑healing boost:** a summer afternoon (or an induction/microwave heater pass, since loaded pores couple strongly to microwaves) triggers a controlled release that closes microcracks — turning "crack sealing" into a heater truck driving over the lane.
- **Free extras:** the pores buffer the moisture that causes stripping and ravelling at the aggregate–binder interface, cation‑exchange sites getter the zinc, copper and PAHs in runoff, and residual porosity reduces tyre noise.
- **It reports its own condition:** each guest desorbs at its own temperature, so a thermal‑desorption ramp on a small core gives a direct measure of remaining rejuvenator and accumulated oxidation — an objective pavement‑life number replacing today's calendar‑based resurfacing schedules.

**Application:** low‑temperature, high‑RAP, low‑fume road construction and airport paving, plus maintenance‑free extension of pavement life in hot climates — a road whose repair chemistry is already mixed into it, locked inside grains of clay‑grade mineral.

**Zeolite "sky ballast" — a pump‑free, solar‑driven altitude‑control organ for stratospheric balloons and airships.**

Long‑duration stratospheric platforms (weather and telecom balloons, wind‑navigated "Loon"‑type craft, high‑altitude solar airships) steer by changing altitude to catch different wind layers. Today that means either dropping sand ballast and venting lift gas — which ends the flight in days — or running an electric air pump against the envelope's superpressure, which costs batteries, motors and the single most common failure point in the vehicle.

**The invention:** replace the pump and the ballast hopper with a lightweight zeolite cartridge (Ca‑A/13X for N₂/O₂, behind a hydrophobic silicalite guard layer) plumbed to the balloon's internal air ballonet, with one face black and sun‑exposed and one face radiating to the −60 °C sky.

- **Descend (day):** sunlight warms the bed to 150–250 °C; the framework desorbs its air charge into the ballonet at three to four orders of magnitude higher pressure than it was captured, inflating the ballast bladder. The craft gains "virtual ballast" — displacement is taken up by heavy air instead of lift gas — and it sinks into a different wind layer. Rate is throttled by a shade louvre or a milliwatt heater, so altitude is *steered*, not merely traded away.
- **Ascend (night, or on command):** the radiator face drops the bed to ambient and the cold pores suck the ballonet air back down to a few millibar — a vacuum pump with no rotor, no seal, no lubricant and no battery, working on exactly the 5 kPa ambient pressures where mechanical pumps are least efficient. The balloon rises.
- **Zero consumables, unlimited cycles:** nothing is dropped, vented or burned; the working fluid is the stratosphere's own air, and the "engine" is the day–night thermal swing that the vehicle experiences anyway. Flight duration stops being set by ballast mass and becomes set by envelope life.
- **Free extras from the same brick:** the adsorption exotherm released at dusk keeps avionics and batteries above their survival temperature (the other classic killer of stratospheric flights); the pores getter the water, CO₂ and ozone that embrittle the envelope film and fog optics; and, in a helium craft, a small Ag⁺/Cs⁺‑exchanged "trapdoor" layer recaptures diffused lift gas from the ballonet rather than letting it be vented.
- **Why zeolite:** a crystalline aluminosilicate is unaffected by −80 °C to +250 °C cycling, hard vacuum, UV and ionising radiation at 20 km, is non‑flammable next to a hydrogen envelope, and cycles tens of thousands of times with no fatigue; the isotherm makes altitude authority a calculable material constant, and a thermistor plus a pressure gauge reads the bed's exact state of charge, i.e. how much "ballast" the vehicle has left.

**Application:** months‑to‑years persistence for stratospheric communications and disaster‑relief relay platforms, wind‑field navigation for climate and ozone sounding, persistent overhead imaging and wildfire watch, and planetary aerobots (a Venus or Titan balloon can run the same cycle on its own atmosphere) — turning altitude control from a battery‑and‑ballast budget into a rock that breathes with the sun.

**Zeolite "cold maser" — pentacene‑in‑channel crystals as a room‑temperature, zero‑noise microwave amplifier.**

Room‑temperature masers exist today only as fragile pentacene‑doped p‑terphenyl crystals: the host melts near 210 °C, cracks under its own pumping heat, cannot be grown large or doped uniformly, and can only be pulsed — which is why the quietest amplifier ever demonstrated has never left the bench.

**The invention:** grow millimetre‑scale crystals (or sinter a transparent ceramic) of a one‑dimensional large‑pore aluminosilicate — AFI/AlPO‑5, ZSM‑12 or L‑type, straight 7–12 Å channels — and thread them, one molecule per unit cell, with pentacene (or a nitroxide/vanadyl spin carrier), then seal the pore mouths with silane "stopcocks."

- **How it lases in the microwave:** a yellow LED/laser pulse pumps pentacene to a triplet state whose spin sublevels are born wildly out of thermal equilibrium. That population inversion, placed in a dielectric or metamaterial resonator inside a modest magnet, gives stimulated emission at a few GHz — amplification with an effective noise temperature below 1 K, but with the crystal sitting at room temperature.
- **Why the zeolite host is the enabling part:** the channel forces every guest into an identical orientation and an identical crystal field, so the spin transition is homogeneous and the gain is a reproducible material constant rather than a doping accident; each molecule is caged and cannot dimerise or be reached by O₂, so triplet quenching and photobleaching — the reason present masers die after minutes — largely stop; and the aluminosilicate is stable past 800 °C with far better thermal conductivity and no melting point, so the pump heat can be conducted away and the device run **continuous‑wave** rather than pulsed. Framework choice and cation exchange shift the zero‑field splitting, i.e. tune the operating frequency without changing the magnet.
- **Free extras:** the mineral is radiation‑hard, non‑outgassing and vacuum‑compatible (so it flies), and the empty fraction of the pore volume getters the water and oxygen that would otherwise poison the guest over decades.

**Applications:** cryogen‑free ultra‑low‑noise front ends for radio telescopes, SETI and deep‑space communication (replacing HEMT amplifiers and their liquid‑helium cryostats); readout amplifiers for superconducting and spin qubits, MRI/NMR and ESR spectrometers, where the amplifier's noise currently sets the signal averaging time; quantum‑limited receivers for radar, satellite ground stations and gravitational‑physics experiments; and, run as an oscillator, a compact maser frequency standard — turning the world's quietest amplifier from a fragile organic crystal into a grain of rock with a molecule locked in every channel.

**Zeolite "stack sponge" — a washwater‑free, regenerable marine exhaust scrubber that turns a ship's sulfur pollution into a saleable product.**

Ships burning heavy fuel either buy expensive low‑sulfur distillate or fit "open‑loop" wet scrubbers that simply wash SO₂ into the sea — an acidic, metal‑ and PAH‑laden discharge now banned in a growing list of ports and coastal states. The invention replaces the wet tower with a dry, low‑back‑pressure ceramic cartridge in the funnel uptake, built as a laminate of tailored frameworks.

- **Guard layer:** a hydrophobic high‑silica (silicalite‑1/Beta) front zone strips the water vapour and hydrocarbon mist that instantly destroy every conventional dry sorbent, and traps the semi‑volatile organics and ultrafine soot that no wet scrubber removes.
- **SOₓ storage:** Ba²⁺/Ca²⁺/Na⁺‑exchanged large‑pore frameworks chemisorb SO₂ and SO₃ on their cation sites as surface sulfite/sulfate down to ppm levels, concentrating them by orders of magnitude inside the pores — the step that makes a dilute, 300 °C flue gas treatable without any liquid at all.
- **NOₓ and soot in the same brick:** a Cu‑ or Fe‑exchanged small‑pore CHA zone oxidises NO to the strongly held NO₂ and, with a trace of urea, runs as a conventional SCR catalyst; catalytic sites also burn the trapped soot off the guard layer at exhaust temperature, so the cartridge is its own particulate filter and its own regenerator.
- **The sulfur becomes cargo, not effluent:** at a modest thermal or vacuum swing driven by the main engine's own waste heat, the bed releases a *concentrated* SO₂ stream that is condensed or catalytically converted to sulfuric acid or elemental sulfur and offloaded in port as a saleable commodity — the same sulfur the refinery removed and charged for, recovered at the point of use instead of dumped in the ocean.
- **Endlessly reusable and auditable:** the aluminosilicate cycles for the life of the vessel (non‑flammable, vibration‑ and salt‑proof, stable past 800 °C, no caustic dosing, no seawater pumps, no sludge), and because desorption is stoichiometric, the sulfur and NOₓ recovered per voyage is a direct, tamper‑resistant emissions log — the compliance evidence port state control currently has to infer from fuel receipts.

**Application:** IMO sulfur‑cap and NOₓ Tier III compliance for merchant ships, ferries and cruise vessels without open‑loop discharge or a switch to costly distillate, plus the same cartridge on port gensets, dredgers, smelters, sinter plants and off‑grid diesel power — turning marine exhaust from a choice between expensive fuel and poisoning the sea into a bed of mineral that hands you back the sulfur.

**Zeolite "shelf‑life clock" — a passive diffusion‑kinetic time‑temperature tag that shows how much life a perishable product has actually got left.**

The tag is a paper‑thin strip containing a single, oriented crystal film (or a packed capillary) of a straight‑channel zeolite — AlPO‑5/AFI, ZSM‑12 or mordenite, 6–12 Å one‑dimensional channels running along the strip — with a reservoir of a coloured or fluorescent guest molecule (a dye, a caged aldehyde, an indicator amine) sealed at one end. Nothing else: no battery, no chip, no chemistry that can be spoofed.

- **The clock is single‑file diffusion.** Once activated (peel a barrier foil at packing), the guest creeps down the channels by single‑file diffusion, producing a sharp, readable colour front that advances a few millimetres over the product's life. Because the guest is confined in a rigid crystallographic channel, its hopping rate obeys a clean Arrhenius law with an activation energy set by pore aperture, Si/Al ratio and cation exchange — so the tag can be **matched to the actual degradation chemistry of the product** (E_a ≈ 60–90 kJ/mol for microbial growth in chilled fish, ~100 kJ/mol for vaccine protein aggregation, lower for frozen goods). A tag that integrates temperature history with the *same* activation energy as the spoilage reaction reads out true remaining shelf life, not "was it ever above 8 °C" — the fatal weakness of every wax‑melt, polymer‑diffusion and enzymatic TTI on the market today.
- **Freeze‑ and abuse‑aware.** A second channel loaded with a different guest and a different E_a runs alongside; the *ratio* of the two front positions distinguishes "long time, cold" from "short time, hot," and a third strip of hydrophilic zeolite records freeze/thaw and humidity excursions that ruin vaccines and produce. Reading is by eye against a printed scale, or by phone camera/handheld Raman for an auditable number.
- **Unspoofable and un‑resettable.** The front cannot be pushed backwards: reversing it would require heating the tag far above the product's tolerance, and doing so leaves a permanent thermal signature in a co‑located "over‑range" framework. There is no electronics to clone, no ink to reprint, and each batch's framework/cation combination is itself a molecular barcode tying the tag to a specific packer and date.
- **Why zeolites rather than polymers or enzymes:** polymer‑diffusion and enzymatic indicators drift with humidity, plasticiser migration, UV and shelf storage, and each production lot behaves slightly differently. A crystalline channel is a reproducible material constant — batch‑independent, humidity‑immune (the hydrophobic frameworks exclude water entirely), unaffected by UV, gamma sterilisation, freezing to −80 °C or a 40 °C warehouse, and stable for years in the *unactivated* state, so tags can be stockpiled anywhere without a cold chain of their own. They are made of clay‑grade minerals at fractions of a cent each.

**Applications:** chilled meat, fish, dairy and fresh produce, where roughly a third of food waste comes from discarding still‑good stock on a printed date while genuinely abused stock is sold; vaccine, insulin and blood‑product distribution in hot and off‑grid regions (a per‑vial, physics‑based replacement for the vaccine‑vial monitor); frozen‑chain verification for seafood and ice cream; pharmaceutical and biologic shipping; adhesive, resin, propellant and battery‑cell ageing tracking in warehouses; and munitions and emergency‑ration stockpiles that must be surveyed without opening them — turning "use by" from a printed guess into a molecule walking down a channel in a grain of mineral at exactly the speed at which the product is actually spoiling.

**Zeolite "frost‑free heat pump" — a rotating sorbent pre‑dryer that stops outdoor coils icing up, killing the defrost cycle.**

Air‑source heat pumps lose 10–25 % of their seasonal efficiency to a single, stupid problem: in cold, damp weather the outdoor evaporator runs below the dew point, water freezes on the fins, airflow chokes, and the machine must periodically **run backwards** — burning the heat it just made (plus resistance backup) to melt its own ice, while the house goes cold and the unit drips a frozen puddle onto the pad.

**The idea:** put a slow‑turning zeolite‑coated wheel (or a pair of switched honeycomb cartridges) in front of the outdoor coil.

- **Dry the air before it ever touches the fins.** A honeycomb coated with a stepped‑isotherm aluminophosphate/SAPO (backed by a Na‑X zone for the deep cut) strips the incoming air's moisture at 0 to –10 °C, where its water affinity is highest. The evaporator now sees dry air, so its surface can sit well below 0 °C and **no ice can form at all** — the defrost cycle, its 4‑way‑valve reversals, its supplementary heater and its drain‑pan heater are all deleted.
- **The regeneration heat is already there, and free.** The loaded half of the wheel is purged with the compressor's discharge‑line/desuperheater heat (60–90 °C) — energy that is otherwise dumped into the house or wasted — and the moist purge air is vented. The stepped isotherm means the sorbent releases fully at that low temperature, unlike silica gel, which needs 120–150 °C.
- **You also get the latent heat back.** Adsorption is strongly exothermic (~3–4 MJ per kg of water), so the air leaving the wheel is several degrees *warmer* as well as drier. That raises the evaporating temperature and the COP directly — the heat pump is partly running on the latent heat of the outdoor air's humidity, which today it can only harvest as a nuisance layer of frost.
- **Same hardware, summer mode.** Reverse the wheel's duty in cooling season and it becomes a desiccant dehumidifier on the *indoor* side: the machine controls humidity independently of temperature, so it no longer has to overcool the air to wring it out, and refrigerant‑side capacity falls with the latent load.
- **Why zeolite rather than silica gel or LiCl:** a crystalline mineral cannot deliquesce, migrate, cake, corrode the aluminium fins or shed dust into the airstream; it tolerates rain, salt spray, UV, insects and 200 °C, works for tens of thousands of cycles, and its steep isotherm makes the drying set point a designed material constant. A cheap dielectric electrode on the wheel reads its water loading, so the controller knows exactly when to purge instead of guessing from a coil thermistor.

**Applications:** cold‑climate residential and commercial air‑source heat pumps — the technology on which most national heating‑decarbonisation plans depend, and whose worst real‑world performance occurs precisely in the near‑freezing, high‑humidity conditions where frosting is worst; plus refrigerated display cases and cold‑room evaporators (whose defrost heaters are a large share of supermarket electricity), transport refrigeration units, and heat‑pump clothes dryers. It turns the heat pump's biggest efficiency leak into a wheel of clay‑grade mineral spun by a 5 W motor.

**Zeolite "clean‑smoke" cartridge — a mineral that separates smoke *flavour* from smoke *carcinogens*, so smoked foods can taste traditional and pass PAH limits.**

Smoking fish, meat, cheese and paprika is one of the oldest food technologies and one of the most heavily regulated: the flavour comes from small lignin‑pyrolysis phenols (guaiacol, syringol, eugenol, cresols) and carbonyls, but the same smoke carries benzo[a]pyrene and the other polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, plus formaldehyde and nitrosamine precursors, which EU/Codex limits now cap so tightly that many traditional smokehouses have had to switch to bland "liquid smoke" or shut down.

**The device:** a swappable ceramic honeycomb between the smoke generator and the smoking chamber, built as a laminate of tailored frameworks.

- **Flavour is admitted, carcinogens are not.** A medium‑pore, moderately hydrophobic dealuminated framework (Beta/mordenite/ZSM‑5 tuned to ~5.5–6.5 Å) swallows the compact, single‑ring phenols and guaiacols — exactly the molecules that carry smoke aroma — while benzo[a]pyrene, benz[a]anthracene, chrysene and the rest of the 4–6‑ring PAHs (kinetic diameters ~8–10 Å, and strongly bound to soot) are size‑excluded and held instead on a sacrificial front layer of macroporous soot trap. What passes into the chamber is a smoke stripped of >95 % of its PAH load but with its phenolic profile intact.
- **The nastier small molecules are dealt with chemically.** A Ca²⁺/Na⁺‑exchanged basic zone chemisorbs formaldehyde and acrolein, and a Cu/Fe‑exchanged zone destroys NOₓ (the nitrosamine precursor in smoked, cured meats) at the flue's own temperature — so the two other regulated hazards of smoking disappear along with the PAHs.
- **Flavour is then *dosed*, not blown.** The loaded bed is warmed and purged with humid air into the smoking chamber, releasing a metered phenol plume whose rate is set by heater power against a known isotherm. Smoking becomes a reproducible recipe — "18 mg guaiacol equivalents per kg, over four hours" — instead of an art dependent on wood moisture, draught and the smoker's nose, and cold‑smoking no longer requires a smouldering fire at all.
- **Blending and terroir.** Separate cartridges loaded from beech, alder, oak, peat or mesquite can be mixed like ink channels, and cation exchange shifts each guest's desorption temperature so "top note" and "base note" smoke compounds arrive on a designed schedule — a physically encoded smoke profile that can be stored dry for years.
- **Regeneration is a burn‑off, and it is the audit trail.** A 450–500 °C air pulse (from the generator itself) oxidises the trapped PAHs and soot inside the pores and returns the honeycomb to full capacity for hundreds of cycles. Because the destroyed material is quantifiable, each cycle yields a direct, auditable record of how much benzo[a]pyrene was removed from a given batch — compliance evidence that today can only be obtained by destructive lab testing of the finished product.
- **Why a zeolite:** a food‑grade, non‑flammable crystalline aluminosilicate that survives 500 °C flue gas, sheds nothing into the food, is unaffected by the tars and 100 % humidity that blind activated carbon in hours, and separates by molecular size rather than by bulk sorption — which is precisely why it can take out the carcinogen and leave the flavour, something no filter, electrostatic precipitator or liquid‑smoke substitute can do.

**Applications:** traditional smokehouses for salmon, herring, ham, bacon, sausage and cheese that must meet PAH limits without losing their product identity; artisanal and export producers in regions where smoked fish is a staple and PAH failures block trade; smoked paprika, tea and malt (including peated whisky malting, where the same phenol/PAH split applies); commercial and domestic barbecue smokers; and a benchtop "flavour cartridge" that lets a restaurant smoke a dish to a specification in minutes — turning food smoking from a trade‑off between taste and toxicology into a separation performed by a bed of reusable mineral.

**Zeolite "gut recorder" capsule — a swallowable, battery‑free mineral pill that maps the chemistry of the entire digestive tract.**
